title: Ceiling Collapses at Kennedy Center: What Happened?
summary:
Have you ever seen a ceiling fall? On Friday night, a chunk of the ceiling fell inside the Kennedy Center in Washington, D.C. The Kennedy Center is a famous place where people go to see music and plays. No one was hurt, but there was a big hole in the ceiling and pieces of it were all over the red carpet.

The center's leaders say this shows why they need to close the building for two years to fix it up. They want to spend $250 million on repairs. The center's board, which is led by President Trump, also wants to put Trump's name on the building. But a judge said that was not allowed and ordered the name to be taken down.

Some people think the ceiling falling is a sign that the building is old and needs fixing. But others, like Grace Terpstra from a group called Keep the KC, think the board is using this small accident as an excuse to close the center. She said, "I think they'll try to make it into a bigger thing."

The ceiling fell during a storm. The center's spokesperson, Roma Daravi, said it shows "the urgent need to close for renovation." She also said the damage happened because "decades of neglect" by past leaders.

So, what do you think? Should the Kennedy Center close for two years to get fixed, even if it means Trump's name goes up? It's a big argument, and people are watching to see what happens next.
why_it_matters: It matters because public buildings like the Kennedy Center belong to everyone, and kids who love music and theater may not get to visit while it is closed for repairs.
